author: Russell Brand
description:
Something is being rolled out across Britain that will cap how much carbon each ordinary person is allowed to produce in a year, and while the government frames this as a collective sacrifice for the planet, there is a very particular group of people who will never feel it. Bill Gates flies private across the world at a rate that would consume the average British person's annual carbon allowance in a single afternoon, and the system built to hold you accountable has a very elegant solution for men like him — just pay for it. Carbon offsetting is the permission slip that turns unlimited consumption into environmental virtue, and the question nobody in power wants you to ask is why the limit only ever seems to land on the people who can least afford it while the architects of the green agenda exempt themselves from it entirely. The rules are for you. The skies are for them.
